sophie (Support): @anna thanks for the report — I can see increased p50/p95 from your app and a spike in 5xxs. Can you share a sample request id?
anna (Customer): thanks, here: req_01H8A3Z2XQY6M3R0. We're pinned to eu-west dedicated pool 'ded-eu-42' but getting 130-300ms extra RTT and occasional 502s.
sophie (Support): looking at logs we see your requests landing on host=hosted-us-east-1 for a subset of tokens. That shouldn't happen if you're pinned.
matt (Infra): possible cause: overflow policy kicked in when ded pool hit soft cap and routing code decided to fall back to hosted. Need to confirm why pinning check failed.
lee (Eng Runtime): can you paste request headers and the X-Route decision log? Also which SDK/version? We've seen older SDKs not sending region header correctly.
anna (Customer): sending curl snippet: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" -d '{"model":"gpt-4r","input":"hi"}'```
sophie (Support): thanks. We see your token tied to dedicated contract id: c_ded_233. But routing table shows last-minute rewrite to hosted variant: model->gpt-4r-hosted.
tabitha (Account): billing flagged a small usage bump to hosted pool, customer got charged at hosted rates for ~12k tokens; we need to reconcile if this should be credited.
matt (Infra): repro plan: simulate sustained concurrent requests to push ded-eu-42 to its soft cap and observe routing decision. I suspect a race in capacity accounting + fallback window (30s).
lee (Eng Runtime): quick mitigation: extend fallback window to 120s for pinned contracts and enforce "no-hosted-fallback" flag for enterprise tokens. I'll open a patch but need QA.
oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026-144: named "dedicated routing overflow -> hosted fallback" assigned to matt, lee.
sophie (Support): repro steps for support/SEs: 1) hit ded pool with 300 concurrent streams 2) watch /internal/routing/decisions for token c_ded_233 3) verify hosted fallback events in trace_id.
anna (Customer): can you confirm auth doesn't change? We saw some 401s when routed to hosted; maybe hosted expects a different audience?
lee (Eng Runtime): good catch — hosted endpoints validate audience claim 'aud: hosted.api' for older tokens. Newer contract tokens include both audiences but legacy ones don't. We'll add token audience check before fallback; if mismatch return 429 with helpful message instead of falling back silently.
sre-bot: Note: scheduled canary of the patch planned in eu-west on 1764416000.
devex (Docs): I'll add a short KB article "Dedicated pool overflow behavior and token audiences" with repro steps + customer-facing mitigation.
tabitha (Account): I've flagged a credit for the customer pending root-cause.
sophie (Support): next actions: matt + lee to push patch and short canary; tabitha to handle credit; devex to draft KB; I'll follow up with anna in 4 hours with status. :thumbsup:
